chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about congratulating the birth of a child, when (should it be done)? So he said: 'He (peace be upon him) said: When Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was born, Jibraeel descended with congratulations upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) on the seventh day, and instructed him to name him, teknonym him, shave his head, perform Aqeeqa for him, and pierce his ear. And similarly, when Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was born, he came to him on the seventh day and instructed him with similar actions.'

He said: And for both of them were two forelocks in the left horn (side of the head), and the piercing was in the right ear in the lobe, and in the left, it was in the upper part of the ear. So the earring (Al-Qurt) was in the right, and the ear-ring (Al-Shanf) in the left.
And it has been reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) left for both of them two forelocks in the middle of the head, and this is more correct than the side (horn).

key_terms.التَّهْنِئَة: Congratulations or congratulatory visitation upon a birth
key_terms.يُكَنِّيَهُ: To teknonym him (give him a kunya)

ai.seo_question: When should the rituals of naming, shaving, and Aqeeqa be performed for a newborn according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the divine origin of birth rituals for the Ahl al-Bayt, establishing the seventh day as the prescribed time for Aqeeqa and naming based on Jibraeel’s instruction to the Prophet. It further provides specific jurisprudential details regarding the placement of ear piercings and forelocks, reflecting the unique status and physical characteristics of Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn as recorded in Shia scholarly tradition. The hadith serves as a primary source for the ritualistic practices (Sunnah) associated with the birth of children in Shia fiqh.
